ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure (1), it is known that $AM\parallel CN$, where point B is a point in the plane and $AB\perp BC$ at point B. Through point B, construct $BD\perp AM$ at point D, and let $\angle BCN=\alpha$. As shown in Figure (2), if points E and F are on $DM$, and $BE$, $BF$, and $CF$ are connected such that $BE$ bisects $\angle ABD$ and $BF$ bisects $\angle DBC$, what is the measure of $\angle EBF$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $DB$, intersect $NC$ at point H, as shown,\\
since $AM\parallel CN$, $BD\perp AM$,\\
therefore $DH\perp NC$.\\
Therefore $\angle BHC=90^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle BCN=\alpha $,\\
therefore $\angle HBC=90^\circ-\alpha $.\\
Since $AB\perp BC$,\\
therefore $\angle ABC=90^\circ$.\\
Therefore $\angle ABD=180^\circ-\angle ABC-\angle HBC=\alpha $.\\
Since $BE$ bisects $\angle ABD$,\\
therefore $\angle DBE=\angle ABE=\frac{1}{2}\alpha $.\\
Since $\angle HBC=90^\circ-\alpha $,\\
therefore $\angle DBC=180^\circ-\angle HBC=90^\circ+\alpha $.\\
Since $BF$ bisects $\angle DBC$,\\
therefore $\angle DBF=\angle CBF=\frac{1}{2}\angle DBC=45^\circ+\frac{1}{2}\alpha $.\\
Therefore $\angle EBF=\angle DBF-\angle DBE=45^\circ+\frac{1}{2}\alpha -\frac{1}{2}\alpha =\boxed{45^\circ}$;
